resources.string: Family alerts: not set up yet
An SMS, WhatsApp message or payment request you are unsure about
Nothing is copied yet. Copy the message first, then tap again.
10 scams that target families in India
Paste or type the message here
Tip: in WhatsApp or Messages, press and hold the message, tap Share, then choose Kawach.

Kawach check: %1$s – %2$s

Message:
%3$s

Please call me before I do anything.
It has several warning signs. Do not pay, do not share any OTP or PIN, and do not open links. Ask your family first.
Do not act on it yet. Ask your family, or call the company on the number from its official website or your passbook.
Kawach did not find a known scam here, but that does not prove it is safe. If it asks for money, an OTP or a PIN, ask your family first.
Already paid or shared an OTP?
Act now. Reporting within the first hour gives the bank the best chance to stop the money.
Call 1930 and give the transaction or UPI reference number.
Call your bank on the number on the back of your card and block it.
Do not pay anyone who promises to get your money back. That is a second scam.
Check a message in one tap
Police, CBI or customs never arrest anyone on a video call and never ask for money to close a case. Cut the call and block the number.
Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN or password, and never block accounts by SMS. Call the number on the back of your card.
You never need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Entering the PIN sends money out. Decline the request.
Nobody can guarantee high daily returns. These groups take your money and disappear. Do not pay to join.
Real jobs never pay you to like videos or rate hotels, and never ask you to pay first. Leave the chat.
You cannot win a lottery you never entered. Real prizes never ask for a fee or tax first.
The electricity office does not send SMS asking you to call an officer tonight. Check your bill on the official APDCL app or website.
Scammers pretend to be a relative in trouble, sometimes with a copied voice. Call the person on their old number before paying.
Do not pay. Paying brings more demands. Block the caller, keep screenshots and report on cybercrime.gov.in. You are not at fault.
Courier companies do not ask for payments or app installs through SMS links. Track only on the official website.
Claims to be police, CBI or an officer
Threatens arrest or a legal case

Tells you to keep it secret
Asks you to move money to a safe account

Asks for your PIN to receive money
Talks about a prize or a fee
Promises guaranteed or very high returns

Threatens to leak a video or photos
Says a parcel is held or undelivered
